correctness.rationale: With probability Haar measure, Parseval on P^3 gives the coefficientwise triangle majorant without changing the L2 energy. For one opposite pair put t=bc and s=b²+c². The z-coefficients of the cube are D³+6Dt, 3b(D²+t), 3c(D²+t), 3b²D, 3c²D, b³, c³. Squaring yields the displayed identity; after the other coordinate is averaged its linear-in-t term is nonnegative by constant-term positivity, and its t² coefficient is strictly positive for s>0. After balancing the pairs, E[(z+z⁻¹)^(2k)]=binom(2k,k) and vanishing odd moments give the stated sixth-moment expansion. Its positive coefficient of X²Y² at fixed X²+Y² forces axis balance when that energy is positive, including if originally one axis vanished. The normalized cubic has exactly one maximum on [0,1] at the stated h*, with all five magnitudes positive. The two cube-frequency collisions force the inverse phase pair relations relative to the center; those relations suffice by Haar invariance. The zero polynomial gives equality trivially. The exact proof does not rely on the frozen polynomial checker or on numerical optimization.
